verdict.rationale: RustDesk documents a relay-based remote path. Clients connect peer to peer when possible and fall back to a relay, which can be the public server or self-hosted via the OSS hbbs/hbbr servers using a compose.yml. A long-time user confirms remote access works without opening ports or using a VPN through their own relay. Some community reports describe slow default relays and difficult connections, but they do not concretely refute the documented relay path. missing for 10: documented port-forward or direct-IP setup, documented VPN path, detailed network/port requirements for self-hosted relay setup, consistent independent corroboration of reliable off-network connectivity.

support.subject: As a power user, I can reach my machine away from home, with the relay, VPN, or port-forward path documented

citations.quote: clients connect peer to peer when they can and fall back to your relay.
a free, open-source ID/rendezvous server (hbbs) and relay server (hbbr) that you can deploy on your own infrastructure.
You can use our rendezvous/relay server, set up your own, or write your own rendezvous/relay server.
